task.name: One data-backed model catalog on a single schema, replacing registry literals and models.custom
task.story_text:
## Why

Model definitions live in two places on two schemas. The shipped default set is Python literals in
the config package; project-declared models use a separate mapping that cannot express capability
or phase eligibility and derives them from tier instead. A third, fully expressive form exists for
inline entries in the enabled list.

Nothing about a model definition is behaviour — each is identity plus routing policy plus endpoint
and cost metadata. What genuinely requires code is the adapter that reaches a provider, because a
provider needs a runner module. That line is already the intended one, but the default model set
currently sits on the code side of it, which is why adding or re-pinning a model that runs on an
existing adapter requires a release, and why the two sources have drifted apart.

## Acceptance criteria

- The shipped default model set loads from data through the same parser that reads
  project-declared models, so both sources produce identical structures and one schema governs
  them.
- Declaring or re-pinning a model that runs on an already-supported adapter requires no code
  change and no release.
- A definition can express identity, transport, tier, capability, cost band, dev capability, phase
  eligibility, endpoint, and cost seeds; no field expressible in the shipped set is inexpressible
  in a project-declared one.
- Adding a provider that has no adapter continues to require code, and attempting to declare one
  in data fails with a message naming the supported adapters.
- Where a project declaration and a shipped definition describe the same canonical identity, the
  resolved entry reports which source supplied each field.
- Configuration written in the format this project uses today continues to load unchanged, so
  adopting the new schema is optional rather than forced by this change landing.
- This change does not rewrite the project's own configuration file. Moving that file onto the new
  schema is separate operator work, sequenced after a release containing this change has been cut
  and deployed, because the process that runs sprints for this repository is an installed release
  rather than the working tree and cannot read a schema it does not yet contain.

## Example

The same model is currently expressible three different ways with three different capabilities:

```
shipped default   _entry("openai", "gpt-5.4", "cli", tier=..., capability=9, phases=...)
                    → full expressiveness, requires a release to change

models.custom     openai/gpt-5.5/cli: {provider, model, transport, tier, input_cost_per_mtok}
                    → no capability, no phase_eligibility; capability derived from tier

enabled inline    {provider, model, transport, routing:{...}, cost:{...}, base_url}
                    → full expressiveness, but a selection list is not a definition surface
```

After this change one of these shapes exists, and the shipped set is expressed in it. Configuration
already written in the other shapes still loads.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 asserts the inline models.enabled nested routing/cost form is 'already fully expressive' and Step 1's field list omits pricing_provenance and cost_rank_basis. It is not expressive enough for the shipped set: config/models.py:_entry accepts both, and pricing.resolve_cost_band_basis (config/pricing.py:64-104) *raises* when a band is neither price-attributable nor explicitly based. Shipped entries such as the Anthropic sonnet/opus shorthands deliberately carry pricing_provenance=None with a declared non-price cost_rank_basis, while _parse_enabled_mapping_entry (load.py:283-290) hardcodes PRICING_PROVENANCE_OPERATOR_DECLARED for any declared cost: block — round-tripping the shipped set through that shape as-is would re-band shorthands off unattributed literals, the exact defect #2217 fixed. Not a blocker only because tests/test_pricing_provenance.py:110/117/128 pin AGENT_REGISTRY provenance and will fail immediately.
  Suggestion: Add explicit pricing_provenance and cost_rank_basis (nullable) to the canonical catalog schema in Step 1, and in Step 2 have the shared parser honor declared values instead of inferring operator-declared attribution; keep the operator-declared inference only on the legacy models.custom / inline compatibility paths.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 lists both config/models.py and config/load.py as homes for the shared canonical parser, but load.py already imports AGENT_REGISTRY from models.py — if the parser that builds AGENT_REGISTRY at import time lives in load.py, that is a circular import. Additionally, _parse_enabled_mapping_entry's semantics are overlay semantics: it consults AGENT_REGISTRY.get(canonical_id) for tier/capability/cost/base_url fallbacks (load.py:265-345), which cannot apply when the parser is what constructs AGENT_REGISTRY.
  Suggestion: Put the canonical parser in config/models.py (or a new leaf module both import) and split it into base parsing (no builtin fallback, used for packaged catalog) and overlay resolution (builtin-aware, used for project declarations).
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 5's file list names src/theforge/model_profiles.py and src/theforge/coordinator/model_profiles_bridge.py, neither of which references registry_source today; the file that actually holds the entry-level reporting surface — config/types.py, where ForgeConfig.model_registry_sources is declared at types.py:1241 — is not listed. The new field-level provenance map needs a ForgeConfig field there, and cli/check_config.py:464-469 is the existing consumer to keep working.
  Suggestion: Include config/types.py (ForgeConfig field) and cli/check_config.py in Step 5's scope; touch the model_profiles modules only if a concrete need surfaces.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.4-cli] Step 2 says to use the current inline models.enabled nested routing/cost shape because it is 'already fully expressive', but the current shipped registry uses metadata that shape does not express today: pricing_provenance and routing.cost_rank_basis in src/theforge/config/models.py:_entry, while src/theforge/config/load.py:_parse_enabled_mapping_entry can only infer operator-declared pricing/banding. If implementation literally reuses the current inline shape unchanged, built-in entries like anthropic/sonnet, deepseek-reasoner, and local OpenAI-compatible models will lose existing routing/accounting semantics.
  Suggestion: Keep the shared-parser approach, but extend the canonical cost schema enough to round-trip current AgentSpec pricing/band metadata rather than treating the existing inline shape as sufficient as-is.
- [P2] [openai-gpt-5.4-cli] Backward-compat in Step 4 should explicitly preserve alias-key resolution for models.custom declarations. Current loader behavior lets models.enabled select a custom declaration by its operator-chosen key and then rewrites it to the canonical identity via _parse_custom_model_registry/overlay_aliases in src/theforge/config/load.py; tests rely on this (tests/test_config_transport_identity.py, tests/test_config_load.py).
  Suggestion: Call out declaration-key alias preservation in the compatibility adapter and add a focused test that models.enabled: ['gpt-5.5'] still resolves to openai/gpt-5.5/cli when declared under models.custom.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
